text: Kestrelline Rail will build its new maintenance depot in Port Ansgar, company and city officials said Wednesday, ending months of speculation over the site. The facility, to be constructed on a 14-acre parcel near the North Quay freight corridor, is expected to support routine servicing for the operator’s coastal fleet and create about 120 permanent jobs once fully open. Groundwork is scheduled to begin in late spring, with the depot projected to enter service in 2027. Mayor Elin Varr said the project “puts Port Ansgar at the center of a growing regional transport network.” Kestrelline Rail said the depot will include inspection bays, parts storage and staff training rooms.
